canonical_alias.note: The draft stores y + long_oo, but the converter collapses that sequence to long_u. Zero matches are a representation mismatch, not proof that English lacks this spelling.

catalog_gap.note: Examples support a missing spelling-family candidate. Confirm the full grapheme and context before adding a definition. The same observed pair may include alignment fragments.

doubled_consonant.note: This doubled spelling has a single consonant sound in the samples. Add or reconcile a base spelling definition and review the boundary rule that excludes many doubled-consonant words. Do not change the existing doubling lesson concept.

context_grouping.note: Evidence mixes genuine vowel alternatives with pieces of larger spellings. Inspect neighboring letters and pronunciation before adding a standalone phonogram.

consonant_le.note: The sampled l, t, d, c or s carries part of an unstressed consonant-le ending. A standalone consonant-to-schwa definition would encode the aligner’s split rather than the intended spelling. Re-align the ending first.

letter_name.note: The sound sequence resembles a spoken letter name or abbreviation expansion. Preserve the word as diagnostic evidence; do not add it as a general phonics spelling without an explicit abbreviation policy.

exception.note: Samples suggest a lexical exception or limited spelling family. Verify each relevant pronunciation and keep any exception word-specific until its teaching policy is approved.

loan_name.note: Samples contain names or loanword spelling candidates. Decide whether these words belong in the tutoring vocabulary before expanding the teaching inventory. Frequency alone cannot decide this.

palatalization.note: Samples show sh, zh, ch or j in a context-dependent spelling or ending. Define the exact letters and context after regrouping; preserve morphology and other existing lesson concepts.

excluded_evidence.note: No mechanically consistent word currently supports this record. Resolve the words’ exclusion reasons before calling the spelling invalid or adding a curriculum definition.

defined_rare.note: A definition already exists, but fewer than ten retained words match it. Check excluded matches and segmentation before deciding this is genuinely rare. Low count is not a defect by itself.

unresolved.note: This candidate remains unresolved after first-pass evidence review. Inspect the listed consistent and excluded examples and compare source pronunciations before making a spelling claim.

silent_punctuation.note: The spelling unit includes punctuation. It belongs in orthographic separator handling, not the phonogram teaching inventory. Spoken punctuation alignments need separate inspection.

silent_grouping.note: A zero-sound unit may be a genuine silent letter or a leftover piece of a larger spelling. Regroup and inspect the full word before treating this as a silent-letter phonogram.
